A few weeks ago I was in a Wal-Mart and I crossed through the toys section. The new Ghostbusters toys caught my attention so I decided to see how they compared to the toys I remembered as a kid. But the thing I noticed right away was there were full racks of the toys. "Not a surprise," I thought, since the movie wouldn't be out for a while. But then I noticed that right next to them were completely empty racks. The tags had the names of the original Ghostbusters, like "Ray" and "Egon". So Ghostbusters certainly WAS current enough to warrant toy purchases, but here was actual market evidence that people just wanted their old favorites, not these un-funny Feig-directed harpies.

Progressive people will try to tell you OVER AND OVER AGAIN that there are under-served demographics in the toy market. They'll complain that little girl Marvel fans aren't getting enough to buy, or that there weren't enough Rey figurines in the Star Wars lineup. In certain small instances they may be correct, but for the most part, they fail to realize that toy lines are risk-averse and governed heavily by decades of hard data. Times do change, but that data changes very little. And cries for "inclusiveness" and other concessions that contradict that data usually result in lost money and bargain-bin liquidation.
